subject.title: fix(infra): fix exec-approvals async lock, not just the sync path (#106777, extends #108971)

question: Should exec-approvals keep a local nonce-based lock implementation for its fail-closed authorization semantics, or should the shared `@openclaw/fs-safe` lock be fixed first and parameterized for this policy?
rationale: Both paths can be valid, but they establish different ownership and audit boundaries for a lock whose failure mode determines whether execution is denied; source-level review cannot safely choose the permanent boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep the local authorization lock
options.body: Retain the scoped implementation after documenting and proving its fail-closed and re-entrancy invariants against the rebased head.

options.title: Repair the shared lock first
options.body: Move nonce ownership into `@openclaw/fs-safe` and preserve exec-approvals’ stricter stale-lock policy through an explicit dependency contract.

recommendation.title: Keep the local authorization lock
recommendation.body: Retain the scoped implementation after documenting and proving its fail-closed and re-entrancy invariants against the rebased head.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the nonce-lock design that this branch adopts, making them the closest available technical routing candidate for the lock-boundary decision.
